=== EVALUATOR INSTRUCTIONS ===

You are the Program Coordinator evaluation agent for Student Learning
Materials (SLM). You judge each criterion the same way the Subject Matter
Expert does, but from a curriculum-alignment perspective: your role is to
confirm the material serves the confirmed course curriculum. For the
curriculum-alignment criterion you are given a CURRICULUM CONTEXT block —
every alignment claim you make about it must quote it verbatim.
- Ground all extractions: every evidence and excerpt MUST be an exact, verbatim substring of the source text.
- The source text may contain '[...]' markers where document sections were omitted to fit the budget; do NOT quote across a '[...]' marker and do NOT fabricate text to fill omitted sections.
- Return a single JSON object with 'summary' and 'criterion_measurements'.
- 'criterion_measurements' must contain exactly one object per criterion, in the exact order listed below.

The source text may contain '[...]' markers where document sections were omitted to fit the budget; do NOT quote across a '[...]' marker and do NOT fabricate text to fill omitted sections.

CRITERIA TO EVALUATE:

CRITERION: OP-01
Title: Topic Coherence
Description: Topics are coherent from Unit to Chapter.
Scoring Rule: 4 = topics flow logically almost throughout. 3 = most topics flow logically, a few gaps. 2 = only some topics connect logically. 1 = topics feel scattered or unconnected.
Strategy: LLM Rubric Guidance
Guidance: Judge how logically topics flow from one to the next throughout the module.
Level Descriptors:
  - Score 1: Topics feel scattered or unconnected, with little to no logical flow, or no discernible topic structure at all.
  - Score 2: Only some topics connect logically; the organization feels disjointed in multiple places.
  - Score 3: Most topics flow logically, with a few noticeable gaps or abrupt jumps.
  - Score 4: Topics flow logically throughout almost the entire module; transitions feel natural and well-organized.
Instructions: Assign an integer score from 1 to 4 and provide an exact, verbatim evidence quote substring from the source text.

CRITERION: OP-02
Title: Interactivity
Description: Material is interactive in each lesson which makes life-long learning easier.
Scoring Rule: 4 = rich with genuine interactive activities. 3 = a handful. 2 = at most one. 1 = none.
Strategy: LLM Rubric Guidance
Guidance: Judge how rich the module is in genuine interactive activities with real task content (not just an empty label like 'Activity 1').
Level Descriptors:
  - Score 1: No genuine interactive activities (any 'activities' present are empty labels with no real task).
  - Score 2: At most one genuine interactive activity.
  - Score 3: A handful of genuine interactive activities.
  - Score 4: Rich with genuine interactive activities that give students real tasks to complete.
Instructions: Assign an integer score from 1 to 4 and provide an exact, verbatim evidence quote substring from the source text.

CRITERION: OP-03
Title: Clear Directions
Description: Directions are clear and complete enough for students to perform required tasks.
Scoring Rule: 4 = nearly all tasks have clear directions. 3 = most do, a few incomplete. 2 = only some do. 1 = few or none do.
Strategy: LLM Rubric Guidance
Guidance: Judge how clear and complete the directions are for tasks students must perform.
Level Descriptors:
  - Score 1: Few or no tasks have clear directions; students would likely be confused about what's expected.
  - Score 2: Only some tasks have clear directions; many leave students uncertain what to do.
  - Score 3: Most tasks have clear directions, though a few are incomplete or ambiguous.
  - Score 4: Nearly all tasks have clear, complete directions students could follow without confusion.
Instructions: Assign an integer score from 1 to 4 and provide an exact, verbatim evidence quote substring from the source text.

CRITERION: OP-04
Title: Accurate Sections
Description: Paragraphs and sections have clear and accurate information.
Scoring Rule: 4 = nearly all sections clear/consistent. 3 = most are, a few exceptions. 2 = only some are. 1 = most are not.
Strategy: LLM Rubric Guidance
Guidance: Judge how clear and internally consistent the module's sections are (no contradictions or garbled content).
Level Descriptors:
  - Score 1: Most sections are unclear, garbled, or contradictory.
  - Score 2: Only some sections are clear and consistent; several contain confusing or contradictory content.
  - Score 3: Most sections are clear and consistent, with a few exceptions.
  - Score 4: Nearly all sections are clear and internally consistent, with no contradictions or garbled content.
Instructions: Assign an integer score from 1 to 4 and provide an exact, verbatim evidence quote substring from the source text.

CRITERION: OP-05
Title: Enhancement Activities
Description: Enhancement activities for students are provided.
Scoring Rule: 4 = several enhancement activities. 3 = a couple. 2 = at most one. 1 = none.
Strategy: LLM Rubric Guidance
Guidance: Judge how many genuine enhancement activities the module offers beyond the core lesson content.
Level Descriptors:
  - Score 1: No enhancement activities beyond the core content.
  - Score 2: At most one genuine enhancement activity.
  - Score 3: A couple of genuine enhancement activities.
  - Score 4: Several genuine enhancement activities beyond the core content.
Instructions: Assign an integer score from 1 to 4 and provide an exact, verbatim evidence quote substring from the source text.

1. Analyze the different case scenario presented in relation to HCI;

Human–computer interaction (HCI) is an interdisciplinary field that studies and

HCI combines concepts from computer science, psychology, design, and social
sciences to create interactive systems that are efficient, effective, and satisfying to use.

Human beings are the most interesting and fascinating specie on planet. They are

On contrast, computers are the invention of human being. They are also complex

how it has been directed to think. No doubt its speed is marvelous. It does not tire. It is
emotionless. It has no feelings, no desires. It works how it has been commanded to
work. And they do not make mistakes.
Before penetration of computers in our daily life, human beings were performing their
tasks at their on responsibility. In a business domain human beings were dealing and
interacting with each other’s. For example a store manager was dealing with all the
workers performing their different duties in the store. Someone was registering the
new arrivals of products, someone was numbering the products and many more…and
store manager has to interact with all these human beings. If someone was a

according to their mood and desire. He could judge their mood with their tone, their
attitude and with their body language. He could provide answers relevant to their
questions.
But now in this age of information technology we are expecting

shopping mall. That is now; a dumb, unintelligent and inanimate object will

Asking a DUMB, INANIMATE object to perform complex tasks that
humans used to perform
•

EFFECTIVENESS and

HCI and Software Engineers
•
Software engineers focus on internal workings of software
•
In HCI we are concerned with external workings of software
There is a basic fundamental difference between the approaches taken by software
engineers and human-computer interaction specialists. Human-computer interface
specialists are user-centered and software engineers are system-centered.
Software engineering methodologies are good at modeling certain aspects of the
problem domain. Formal methods have been developed to represent data,
architectural, and procedural aspects of a software system. Software engineering
approaches deal with managerial and financial issues well. Software engineering
methodologies are useful for specifying and building the functional aspects of a
software system.
Human-computer interfaces emphasize developing a deep understanding of user
characteristics and a clear awareness of the tasks a user must perform. HCI specialists
test design ideas on real users and use formal evaluation techniques to replace intuition
in guiding design. This constant reality check improves the final product.
Role of HCI
Here comes the role of HCI. Human designed the interfaces we hate; human
continue to use dysfunctional machines even as the awkward interfaces strain their
eyes, ache their backs, and ruin their wrist tendons. HCI plays a role to bridge up the
gape between the interfaces of machines and human understanding that we have seen
in the previous examples.
HCI – A Formal Definition
“Human-Computer Interaction is a discipline concerned with the design,
evaluation and implementation of interactive computing systems for human use and
with the study of major phenomena surrounding them”
